sections.title: Identifying risks
sections.content:
Vocabulary for discussing danger and risk:
• hazard — a danger or risk. Wet floors are a serious slip hazard.
• vulnerable — at risk of harm. Elderly people are particularly vulnerable to extreme heat.
• jeopardise — put at risk. Leaking the information could jeopardise the entire operation.
• prone to — likely to experience something negative. The area is prone to flooding in winter.
• reckless — without thinking of consequences. Reckless driving is the leading cause of road accidents.

sections.title: Safety and protection
sections.content:
How we describe staying safe:
• precaution — a preventive measure. Take precautions against sunburn when outdoors.
• safeguard — protect from harm. Strong passwords safeguard your personal data.
• eliminate — completely remove a risk. New technology could eliminate many workplace hazards.
• mitigate — make less severe or serious. Wearing seatbelts mitigates the risk of injury.
• compliance — following rules or standards. Companies must ensure compliance with safety regulations.

exercises.question: Someone easily harmed or affected is:
exercises.explanation: Vulnerable means susceptible to physical or emotional harm.

exercises.question: A preventive action taken to avoid danger is a:
exercises.explanation: A precaution is a measure taken in advance to prevent something harmful.

exercises.question: To put something at risk is to:
exercises.explanation: Jeopardise means to put something into a situation of risk or danger.

exercises.question: Acting without considering consequences is:
exercises.explanation: Reckless means acting without thought for the consequences.

exercises.question: To reduce the severity of a risk is to:
exercises.explanation: Mitigate means to make less severe, serious, or painful.

exercises.question: Following rules and regulations is:
exercises.explanation: Compliance is the act of following rules, laws, or standards.

exercises.question: To completely remove a danger is to:
exercises.explanation: Eliminate means to completely remove or get rid of something.

exercises.question: A source of danger in the environment is a:
exercises.explanation: A hazard is a danger or risk to safety.
